Offline checkpoint scoring is now implemented and verified without changing fitting numerics. Eleven focused tests cover raw/map provenance, wrong-state receipts, admission from offline results, pending exports, native rejection, construction/process failures, omitted states and failed fits with no events. The original OASIS 11 coarse-start and fine-start checkpoints reproduce every scientific score exactly; six complete evaluator/anatomy/cell reports are byte-identical. Only audit walltimes and relocated paths to identical hashed intensity inputs are excluded. All 30 scalar events remain accounted for (2 scored, 17 uncaptured, 11 outside the declared two-state export pilot). Compact evidence and reproduction sources are in docs/benchmarks/evidence/halfflow-deferred-capture-20261014/offline-scoring-supplement-v1/; its 137-identity manifest verifies 113 copied files and preserves the original archive manifest unchanged.

The deferred OASIS 11 step-scaled replay finished with exit 0, 16 saved states and exact equality of all four historical final map/validity artifacts. This is process completion, not optimizer convergence. A frozen first offline batch includes all 29 captured states across OASIS 11 selected-control and step-scaled policies; separate one-worker export and scoring processes are now running while the remaining trajectory fits continue. Explicit terminal fit batches retain every selected fit outcome, including failed zero-event fits, and do not remove other fits from the full panel denominator. No D01 gate is closed and no new optimizer policy, fresh qualification data or numerical tolerance change is introduced. Publication remains local pending the previously requested specific evidence-egress approval.
